newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco lawyer says Congress to review FDA role.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco lawyer says Congress to review FDA role.

text.p: A tobacco company lawyer told a Senate panel Thursday that the industry recognizes Congress will want to review and attempt to change how the proposed settlement deals with Food and Drug Administration authority over nicotine.
The accord reached on Friday recognizes FDA jurisdiction over tobacco products but public health advocates say the precise wording actually undermines government regulation.

Meyer Koplow, a private New York lawyer representing Philip Morris said the industry during the negotiations recognized that issues pertaining to the regulation of nicotine "was an issue for Congress to deal with".

Under questioning by the Senate Judiciary committee, the first Congressional panel to start reviewing the proposed $368 billion settlement, Koplow repeatedly refused to say what parts of the agreement the industry could accept changes in and which provisions must remain as drafted.

When Vermont Sen. Patrick Leahy, a Democrat, repeatedly asked if the settlement proposal was a "take it or leave it deal," Koplow said. "We recognize and understand this will go through the legislative process."

Koplow, Mississippi Attorney General Michael Moore and Matthew Myers, the general counsel for the anti-smoking National Center for Tobacco-Free Kids, all defended the overall proposal although all acknowledged that the pact was a compromise. Myers acknowledged that public health advocates were legitimately concerned about fine-print restrictions on FDA authority.
